final_answer: Depth-first search (DFS) explores as far as possible along each branch before backtracking, while breadth-first search (BFS) explores all neighbors level by level. DFS uses a stack, making it suitable for deep graphs or when you want to find any path quickly (e.g., cycle detection). BFS uses a queue and is better for finding the shortest path in unweighted graphs or when the goal is near the root. Choose DFS for deep structures or when memory is tight, and BFS for shortest-path problems or level-wise exploration.
